title: Personal Trading Policy – PNI Securities

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board, seeking approval for their own trading; approved by the Chair of the ACRMC, or the Managing Director in the Chair of the ACRMC's absence.

tiers.name: PNI Directors, KMP and Company Secretary
tiers.description: Directors (other than the Chair), Key Management Personnel and the Company Secretary; approved by the Chair of the Board, or the Chair of the ACRMC in the Chair's absence.

tiers.name: All other Personnel
tiers.description: Employees, consultants and contractors of the Group other than Directors, KMP and the Company Secretary; approved by the PNI Company Secretary, or the Chief Financial Officer in their absence.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Close family members over whom a Personnel member has influence (including spouse/partner and children), any company or trust the Personnel member controls or has an interest in, and any superannuation fund or account the Personnel member has an interest in or can instruct trading decisions for (e.g. SMSF). The Board may derogate the Policy's application to a specific Associate on application, only where there is no actual, potential or apparent conflict of interest.

definitions.hedging_definition: a hedging arrangement aimed at limiting exposure in relation to part of their "at risk" remuneration

windows.end_anchor: 5pm on the first full trading day following the announcement to the ASX of PNI's annual financial results
5pm on the first full trading day following the announcement to the ASX of PNI's half-yearly financial results

rules.detail: "Security" expressly includes options, stock specific derivatives and derivatives (both OTC and exchange traded); "trading" (applying for, acquiring or disposing of, or agreeing to do so) requires prior approval from the relevant authorising officer under section 5, the same as any other trade. There is no outright derivatives ban and no venue distinction.
rules.evidence: Security ... options, stock specific derivatives, derivatives (both over the counter (OTC) and exchange traded), warrants, contracts for difference (CFDs)

rules.detail: The hedging ban is scoped to securities forming part of a Personnel member's "at risk" remuneration (i.e. incentive equity), not the entirety of their PNI shareholding; the Policy does not state whether this is limited to unvested or performance-tested holdings.
rules.evidence: Personnel must not trade in PNI Securities as part of a hedging arrangement aimed at limiting exposure in relation to part of their "at risk" remuneration.

rules.detail: Ordinary vested, unrestricted PNI shares not forming part of "at risk" remuneration are not covered by the hedging-specific ban. Entering a hedge over them is a disposal or agreement to deal that is "trading" and so only requires standard prior written approval, outside a Fixed Prohibited Period.
rules.evidence: All Personnel must seek prior approval from their authorising officer(s) in relation to trading (either personally or through an Associate)

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is "disposing of" a Security or an agreement to do so and is therefore trading requiring prior approval.
rules.evidence: trading ... in relation to a Security, applying for, acquiring or disposing of (or entering into an agreement to do so) the Security.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named and there is no express prohibition; only the 2-month minimum holding period and standard trade approval would apply to any disposal.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are expressly named within the definition of Security, so trading a CFD requires the same prior approval as any other trade; not separately banned.

Margin lending is discouraged but not prohibited. Personnel must disclose a proposed margin lending arrangement to the Company Secretary (who informs the Board) before entering it, and must obtain prior written approval to transfer PNI Securities into a margin loan account; PNI may impose its own conditions on the approval.
rules.evidence: PNI discourages the use of leveraged margin lending arrangements and other secured financing arrangements by Personnel in relation to PNI Securities but has not prohibited their use.

rules.detail: Granting a security interest over PNI Securities as part of a secured financing arrangement expressly requires prior written approval and prior disclosure to the Company Secretary/Board.
rules.evidence: seek prior written approval in accordance with section 6.1 to transferring PNI Securities into a margin loan account or granting a security over PNI Securities as part of a secured financing arrangement.

rules.detail: Any secured financing arrangement in respect of PNI Securities, not limited to margin loans, is discouraged but permitted subject to prior disclosure to the Company Secretary/Board and prior written approval; PNI can attach conditions, including on circumstances for a margin-call sale.
rules.evidence: disclose details of any proposed margin lending arrangement or proposed secured financing arrangement in respect of PNI Securities, and when PNI Securities are to be sold to make repayments under such arrangements, to the PNI Company Secretary who will inform the Board before ... the Personnel member enters into it

rules.detail: A flat 2-month minimum holding period applies from acquisition; buying more PNI Securities while an existing holding is in place resets the 2-month period across the entire holding (new and existing). Does not apply to securities received via involuntary corporate actions or vesting. A written derogation request may be lodged with the Authorising Officer (e.g. on financial hardship grounds).
rules.evidence: PNI Securities must be held for a minimum period of 2 months. ... Where there is an existing holding and more PNI Securities are purchased, the holding period is 2 months for all new and existing PNI Securities.

financing_disclosure: All Personnel: trigger = inception (before entering a margin lending or secured financing arrangement, or before PNI Securities are sold to make repayments under one); to = PNI Company Secretary, who informs the Board; deadline = before the Personnel member enters into it (section 4).

Directors: trigger = a change in the Director's interest in Securities, or the Board determining the arrangement would have a material effect on price or value (threshold); to = ASX; deadline = per Listing Rule disclosure timing, not further specified (section 4).

external_documents: Policy Derogation Register (maintained by Risk & Compliance)
MCO – the Group's governance, risk and compliance system (used for trade approval requests and confirmations)
exemption_authority: Chair of the Board (or Chair of the ACRMC in the Chair's absence, or the Chair's own trading) may grant written approval to sell or otherwise dispose of (not acquire) PNI Securities during a Fixed Prohibited Period for severe financial hardship, legal/court compulsion, or other circumstances they determine exceptional, provided the transaction is lawful, not short-term/speculative, doesn't use Inside Information and won't appear unfair to the market. The Board may also derogate the Policy's application to a Personnel member's Associate where there is no conflict of interest, and the ACRMC approves amendments to the Policy itself.
jurisdiction_overlays: Local rules and regulations of jurisdictions other than Australia, which prevail over this Policy where more stringent (no specific overseas regime named)

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban scoped to at-risk remuneration
bespoke_clauses.clause: Personnel must not trade in PNI Securities as part of a hedging arrangement aimed at limiting exposure in relation to part of their "at risk" remuneration.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike a blanket hedging ban, this only reaches securities forming part of incentive remuneration; a collar over ordinary vested, unrestricted, non-incentive PNI shares is not caught by the hedging prohibition and only needs standard trade pre-clearance, making a funded collar structurally available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where there is an existing holding and more PNI Securities are purchased, the holding period is 2 months for all new and existing PNI Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any top-up purchase during the life of a collar (e.g. under a DRP variation, though DRP participation is itself blocked in Fixed Prohibited Periods) would restart the 2-month minimum hold across the whole collared position, delaying a permitted unwind.

bespoke_clauses.clause: PNI discourages the use of leveraged margin lending arrangements and other secured financing arrangements by Personnel in relation to PNI Securities but has not prohibited their use.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares is permitted in principle, but is subject to prior disclosure to the Company Secretary/Board, prior written approval, and PNI's discretion to impose its own conditions on the facility, including on forced-sale triggers.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Disclosure of a Director's margin lending or secured financing arrangement will be required to be made to the ASX if there is a change in the Director's interest in Securities or if the Board determines that the existence of such arrangement would have a material effect on the price or value of Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director entering a funded collar may need to make a separate ASX disclosure of the financing arrangement itself, beyond the standard Appendix 3Y change-of-interest notice for the derivative legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: trading wholly initiated by a party independent to the Personnel member (e.g. a margin call related sale of stock initiated by the margin lender)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default or margin call does not itself require fresh trading approval, giving the lender a clearer path to enforce security over the collared shares.

summary: A funded collar is achievable under this policy, subject to conditions. The hedging prohibition in section 4 is narrow: it only bans hedging arrangements tied to a Personnel member's "at risk" remuneration, so entering a collar over ordinary vested, unrestricted PNI shares is not itself banned and instead only needs standard prior written approval from the relevant authorising officer (Chair of the ACRMC for the Chair of the Board; Chair of the Board for other Directors/KMP/Company Secretary; Company Secretary for other Personnel), valid for 5 business days, outside the two Fixed Prohibited Periods and while not in possession of Inside Information. The financing leg is expressly permitted, though discouraged: entering a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement, or granting security over the shares, requires prior disclosure to the Company Secretary (who informs the Board) and prior written approval, and PNI may impose its own conditions, including on the circumstances of a margin-call sale; a lender's independently initiated enforcement sale does not itself need approval. Directors' financing arrangements may trigger a separate ASX disclosure obligation if they change the Director's interest or are assessed as material. The main structural constraints are the two Fixed Prohibited Periods, the 2-month minimum holding period (which resets across the whole holding on any new purchase), and PNI's broad discretion to refuse or condition approval and to withdraw it on a change of circumstances.
